Specification of Communication Management AUTOSAR AP R25-11 invocations are processed. The selection is valid for all the methods of the specific ServiceSkeleton instance. The Method Call Processing Mode is set as a parame- ter of the ServiceSkeleton constructor defined by [SWS_CM_00130]. [SWS_CM_10411] Service method processing modes Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00211 ⌈ The following service method processing modes shall be supported: • Polling : Instead of calling a provided service method, the Communication Man- agement software collects incoming service method invocations. The processing of each invocation is explicitly triggered by the implementation providing the ser- vice method using the mechanism defined in [SWS_CM_00199]. • Event-driven, concurrent : The Communication Management software activates the invoked service method when the invocation arrives. Consumer concurrent calls are allowed and will be processed concurrently on provider side by using different threads. This is the default mode. • Event-driven, sequential : The Communication Management software activates the invoked service method when the invocation arrives. Consumer concurrent calls are allowed, but will not be processed concurrently on provider side, by instead executing them one after the other to avoid the need of synchronization mechanisms in the implementation providing the service method. ⌋ The ProcessNextMethodCall() defined in [SWS_CM_00199] allows the imple- mentation providing the service method to trigger the execution of the next service con- sumer method call at a specific point of time if the processing mode is set to Polling . 7.5.7 Registering handler with null pointer [SWS_CM_10417] Register handlers failure due to null pointer or empty function. Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00217, RS_CM_00218, RS_CM_00219 ⌈ Passing a nullptr or an empty std::function as argument to the following ara::com methods is not allowed and shall be handled as violation : • RegisterGetHandler ([SWS_CM_00114], [SWS_CM_11360]) • RegisterSetHandler ([SWS_CM_00116], [SWS_CM_11362]) • SetSubscriptionStateChangeHandler ([SWS_CM_00333], [SWS_CM_11354], [SWS_CM_12008], [SWS_CM_12009]) • SetReceiveHandler ([SWS_CM_00181], [SWS_CM_11356], [SWS_CM_00250], [SWS_CM_00352]) 285 of 675 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement

Specification of Communication Management AUTOSAR AP R25-11 [SWS_CM_00313] Call SubscriptionStateChangeHandler with kSubscription- Pending on the Proxy side Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00103, RS_CM_00104, RS_CM_00106, RS_CM_00107 ⌈ The Communication Management shall call the SubscriptionStateChangeHan- dler on the Proxy side with the value kSubscriptionPending in the following cases: • the client subscribes to an event and the actual subscription does not happen immediately (e.g. due to a bus protocol) • the client is subscribed to an event and Communication Management has de- tected that the server instance is currently not available (due to restart, network problem or so) ⌋ [SWS_CM_12006] Asynchronous nature of Subscribe() Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00106, RS_CM_00107 ⌈ In order to keep application functionality robust against Network Binding configuration changes, applications shall assume asynchronous operation when calling Subscribe . This implies not assuming success in the subscription process until GetSubscrip- tionState() or the handler set by SetSubscriptionStateChangeHandler() have reported kSubscribed , even if Subscribe() has returned with no error. ⌋ [SWS_CM_00085] Precondition for Event/Field unsubscription ⌈ To avoid dangling references to Event sample data (referred to by a ara::com::SamplePtr ) which has not yet been handed back to communication management by the application, it is required that all SamplePtr s provided by GetNewSamples() are released (by calling any of the APIs defined in [SWS_CM_11547], [SWS_CM_11539], [SWS_CM_11540], or [SWS_CM_11545]) before before calling Unsubscribe() . If this precondition is not met, a violation shall be raised as per [SWS_CORE_00090]. ⌋ Note: Special care needs to be taken when an event receive handle calls GetNewSam- ples() - it might lead to violation if an event is received directly before or at the be- ginning of the Unsubscribe() call. [SWS_CM_00314] Call SubscriptionStateChangeHandler with kSubscribed on the Proxy side Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00103, RS_CM_00104, RS_CM_00106, RS_CM_00107 ⌈ The Communication Management shall call the SubscriptionStateChangeHan- dler on the Proxy side with the value kSubscribed in the following cases: • the client subscribes to an event and the actual subscription is established suc- cessfully 291 of 675 Document ID 717: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_CommunicationManagement

Specification of Communication Management AUTOSAR AP R25-11 [SWS_CM_00140] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for transmission requests for Triggers ⌈ To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each trigger shall have a configurable Minimum Send Interval (see ServiceInterfaceDeploymentEle- ment . minimumSendInterval ), which specifies the minimum amount of time that shall pass between two consecutive transmissions, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval limits the maximum Tx frequency of a given trigger in the network. If the application requests transmission of a trigger by calling Trigger::Send()/Send() , ara::com shall check, whether the time since the last successful handover of the trigger to the underlying transmission layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval is not violated. If the trigger has never been sent before, this shall also successfully pass the Minimum Send Interval check. If the Minimum Send Interval is not violated, ara::com shall process the transmission request by handing over the trigger to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new Minimum Send Interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is vio- lated, ara::com shall discard the transmission request and return error ComErrc:: kMinimumSendIntervalViolationError (see [SWS_CM_10432]). If the config- ured Minimum Send Interval ( ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimum- SendInterval ) of a trigger has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding trigger. ⌋ [SWS_CM_00142] Default value of Minimum Send Interval and disabling Mini- mum Send Interval monitoring for Triggers ⌈ If the configured Minimum Send Inter- val ( ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval ) of a trig- ger has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding trigger, i.e., ara::com will not limit the Tx frequency by dropping trans- mission requests. For each Trigger of a ServiceInterfaceDeployment (or the associated Event), 0 shall be the default value for the corresponding ServiceInter- faceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval . This means that unless Ser- viceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval for a given event is explicitly configured to be > 0, the Tx rate is not limited by ara::com . ⌋ 7.5.17 Service trigger subscription For the service trigger subscription C++ API reference, see chapter 8.3.7.1.3.
